paras: The attempted lynching of Tom Chambers was a night attack by a white "vigilance committee" on a Black man at his home on the Tennessee side of Fulton in August 1890. Chambers fought off the band with a hatchet and a knife, and a rope with a hangman's knot found the next morning was taken as the purpose of the visit.
Chambers had testified against some Fulton merchants who were arrested for selling whisky illegally, a point the report placed directly after its account of the attack.

According to the Fulton Argus, a vigilance committee came to Chambers's house on a Friday night, and when he went to the door to ask what they wanted, the men grabbed at him. He slipped their grasp, picked up a hatchet and struck one of the attackers two or three times, saying the man "acted like a chicken with its head cut off." When a second man attacked him, Chambers stabbed him with a knife. The next morning a rope with a hangman's knot was found, which the paper said revealed "the cause of the visit."

Chambers said the men were white and that he knew them. The Argus understood that he had given Tennessee officials the names of the "lynch gang" and meant to have them arrested, but added that "as yet nothing has been done." No report of arrests, charges or the condition of the wounded men was found in the coverage.

The only known account is a Fulton Argus item reprinted by the Hickman Courier of Hickman, Kentucky, on August 29, 1890, under the headline "Vigilants Repulsed." The item told the story largely from Chambers's side and called his attackers a "lynch gang" without defending them, while referring to Chambers as "colored" and "the darkey who testified against some merchants." No coverage of the attack was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Tom Chambers
bases: A band described as a 'vigilance committee' and 'lynch gang' came to Chambers's house at night and grabbed at him, and a rope with a hangman's knot was found the next morning (A2).

Chambers fought off his attackers and was not killed, so the episode was at most an attempted lynching; the only account gives no number of men beyond at least two assailants and states no motive, though it notes he had testified against Fulton merchants (A2).
The only report is one Hickman Courier item reprinted from the Fulton Argus, which relays Chambers's own account (A2).

accounts.label: Fulton Argus, relaying Chambers's account
accounts.gist: A vigilance committee came to Chambers's door at night and grabbed at him; he wounded two with a hatchet and knife, and a hangman's rope found the next morning showed the purpose of the visit. Chambers said the men were white and that he knew them.

framing.detail: The Argus item, reprinted by the Hickman Courier as 'Vigilants Repulsed', called the band a 'lynch gang' and told of Chambers's defense without censure, while calling him 'the darkey who testified against some merchants'.

quotes: Last Friday night Tom Chambers, colored, living on the Tennessee side of Fulton, was visited by a vigilance committee.
The next morning the cause of the visit was ascertained by the finding of a rope with a hangman's knot in it.
Chambers is the darkey who testified against some merchants in Fulton, who were arrested for selling whisky illegally.
We understand he has given the Tennessee officials the names of the "lynch gang," and that he will have them arrested.
